title: Crèche Second Term
overview: Second-Term Curriculum Intent First Term established SECURITY -> RELATIONSHIP -> COMMUNICATION -> MOVEMENT -> EXPLORATION -> ROUTINE -> INDEPENDENCE. Second Term deliberately progresses towards SECURITY -> PARTICIPATION -> COMMUNICATION -> CURIOSITY -> CHOICE -> INCREASING INDEPENDENCE. The child moves from simply experiencing the environment towards participating purposefully within it. Progression From First Term First Term Second Term Progression Respond to familiar words Understand and use more words Explore alongside others Participate increasingly with others Follow familiar routines Anticipate and contribute to routines Carry with support Carry and restore more independently Explore sensory materials Notice and compare properties Experience quantity Notice simple quantity differences Recognise familiar places Notice features of the wider community Participate in self-care Attempt familiar self-care Listen to stories Anticipate and respond to familiar stories Explore materials Make choices about materials Notice nature Participate in caring for the environment Second-Term Curriculum Map Week Big Idea Main Development 1 Weather and My Day Weather awareness and daily routines 2 Sun, Rain and What We Wear Environment, clothing and self-care 3 People Who Help Me Familiar community relationships 4 Helpers at Work Occupations, tools and role play 5 Things That Move Transport, movement and sound 6 Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility Review and responsive curriculum 7 Journeys and Places Position, movement and familiar journeys 8 Food I Know Food vocabulary, senses and healthy experiences 9 Farms and Markets Food origins and Nigerian community life 10 Building and Making Materials, construction and problem-solving 11 Nigeria - My Home Identity, culture, music and environment 12 Music, Art and Celebration Creative expression and cultural experience 13 Look What I Can Do Reflection, independence and term closure Second-Term Language Progression Adults increasingly model expanded sentences such as 'The car is moving', 'The big bus', 'Your shirt is wet', 'The rain is falling' and 'You put three blocks on'. Children are not required to repeat adult sentences; adults provide rich language worth growing into. Second-Term Mathematics Spine Children encounter matching, sorting, one/more, quantity, big/small, full/empty, in/out, on/off, up/down, near/far, fast/slow, shape, space, pattern, size, fitting, stacking and simple sequencing. The progression is EXPERIENCE -> NOTICE -> COMPARE, not worksheet -> memorisation -> test. Second-Term Literacy Entitlement Daily literacy continues through high-quality picture books, songs, rhymes, conversation, sound discrimination, environmental sounds, repeated refrains, story anticipation, picture discussion, meaningful name exposure, scribbling, drawing, large mark-making and fine-motor development. There remains no formal SSP programme for Crèche. Continuous Provision Provide ongoing access to books, construction, small world, home/role play, mathematics, creative materials, Practical Life, sensory experiences and outdoor provision. Enhanced provision changes according to curriculum intent. Practical Life Progression Second Term expects more participation than First Term: CHILD PARTICIPATES AND ATTEMPTS. Experiences include carrying a cup, using a spoon, wiping a small spill, placing a bag, restoring toys, carrying a basket, watering plants, transferring objects, attempting clothing, helping prepare food and sweeping with child-sized equipment. The aim is increasing capability, not perfect performance. Christian Character Spine Second Term deliberately develops Gratitude, Responsibility, Service, Respect, Patience, Thankfulness, Perseverance, Respect for Identity, and Joy/Community. Values should be modelled and practised rather than merely recited. Nigerian and Local Knowledge Children increasingly encounter Owo, school surroundings, local weather, roads, vehicles, community workers, markets, farm produce, foods, music, clothing, stories, families and Nigerian cultural experiences. START WITH THE CHILD'S REAL WORLD - THEN GRADUALLY WIDEN IT. Inclusion and SEND Adapt materials, position, time, adult support, sensory load, language and method of response according to communication access, home language, sensory needs, physical access, emotional regulation, attention, hearing/vision concerns, feeding needs, developmental variation and strengths. Do not remove meaningful curriculum participation unnecessarily. Parent Partnership Home connections may include talking about weather, allowing the child to help choose clothing, naming trusted helpers, noticing vehicles, talking during journeys, naming foods, visiting familiar markets safely, safe household sorting, building with boxes, listening to Nigerian music, sharing family stories and encouraging self-care. HOME LEARNING IS NOT CRÈCHE HOMEWORK. End-of-Second-Term Expectations Depending on age, starting point and individual development, children should show increasing evidence of security with familiar adults; participation in routines; understanding of everyday language; growing expressive communication; interest in books and songs; physical confidence; hand control; self-care participation; simple matching and sorting; awareness of quantity and size; recognition of familiar people, occupations and transport; interest in food, nature and community; constructive and creative exploration; cultural belonging; participation alongside peers; resource restoration; and increasing independence. These are developmental curriculum expectations, not pass/fail criteria. Progression Into Third Term At the end of Second Term, the curriculum moves from I AM SAFE to I PARTICIPATE and increasingly towards I CAN EXPLORE WITH PURPOSE. Third Term can deepen growth and change, water, habitats, small creatures, cause and effect, simple technology, Africa and the wider world, problem-solving, communication and transition.

weeks.title: Weather and My Day
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children notice simple changes in weather and connect them with everyday experiences.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 1 - Weather and My Day

items.title: Weather awareness and daily routines
items.learningIntent: Children notice simple changes in weather and connect them with everyday experiences.
items.learningContent:
Children notice simple changes in weather and connect them with everyday experiences. Vocabulary: sun, rain, hot, wet, dry, sky,
outside, today. Adults model meaningful sentences, maintain predictable routines, use weather books and songs, and explore
wet/dry, full/empty, more/less and simple first/then sequences. Children look outside daily and notice sunshine, rain, clouds and
wind. Practical Life includes wiping safe spills and carrying belongings. Character: Gratitude. Use weather actually experienced in
Owo.
items.teachingGuidance:
Adults model meaningful sentences, maintain predictable routines, use weather books and songs, and explore
wet/dry, full/empty, more/less and simple first/then sequences.
items.outdoorLearning:
Vocabulary: sun, rain, hot, wet, dry, sky,
outside, today.
items.practicalLife: wiping safe spills and carrying belongings
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Use weather actually experienced in
Owo.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 1 - Weather and My Day

weeks.title: Sun, Rain and What We Wear
weeks.bigIdea: Sun, Rain and What We Wear
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children connect weather with simple everyday choices.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 2 - Sun, Rain and What We Wear

items.title: Environment, clothing and self-care
items.learningIntent: Children connect weather with simple everyday choices.
items.learningContent:
Children connect weather with simple everyday choices. Vocabulary: shirt, shoes, hat, clothes, wear, wet, dry, hot, rain. Encourage
dressing participation, pulling, pushing, lifting arms and attempting shoes. Match pairs such as shoes/socks and sort by visible
property. Explore simple reasons for umbrellas, light clothing and footwear. Practical Life: WATCH -> HELP -> TRY. Character:
Responsibility.
items.outdoorLearning: Vocabulary: shirt, shoes, hat, clothes, wear, wet, dry, hot, rain.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 2 - Sun, Rain and What We Wear

weeks.title: People Who Help Me
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children recognise familiar people who help at home, school and in the community.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 3 - People Who Help Me

items.title: Familiar community relationships
items.learningIntent: Children recognise familiar people who help at home, school and in the community.
items.learningContent:
Children recognise familiar people who help at home, school and in the community. Vocabulary: teacher, parent, doctor, nurse,
driver, cleaner, helper, help, care. Teach trusted/familiar adults rather than implying all adults are safe. Use books, actual school
photographs where appropriate, role play and simple person/object matching. Character: Service.
items.teachingGuidance: Teach trusted/familiar adults rather than implying all adults are safe.
items.parentHomeConnection: Children recognise familiar people who help at home, school and in the community.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 3 - People Who Help Me

weeks.title: Helpers at Work
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children notice that people use different objects and tools to perform jobs.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 4 - Helpers at Work

items.title: Occupations, tools and role play
items.learningIntent: Children notice that people use different objects and tools to perform jobs.
items.learningContent:
Children notice that people use different objects and tools to perform jobs. Vocabulary: work, tool, broom, book, car, bag, clean, fix,
drive, teach. Provide safe real objects, sweeping, carrying, transferring, matching and sorting. Include familiar Owo occupations
such as teachers, traders, farmers, healthcare workers, drivers and craftspeople. Character: Service and Respect.
items.teachingGuidance: Children notice that people use different objects and tools to perform jobs.
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Include familiar Owo occupations
such as teachers, traders, farmers, healthcare workers, drivers and craftspeople.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 4 - Helpers at Work

weeks.title: Things That Move
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children investigate familiar transport through movement, sound and play.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 5 - Things That Move

items.title: Transport, movement and sound
items.learningIntent: Children investigate familiar transport through movement, sound and play.
items.learningContent:
Children investigate familiar transport through movement, sound and play. Vocabulary: car, bus, bike, motorcycle, truck, wheel,
move, stop, go, fast, slow. Use push/pull toys, wheels, stop/go games, vehicle books, sounds, printing and box construction.
Introduce simple road-awareness language: stop, hold hands, wait, adult.
items.teachingGuidance: Use push/pull toys, wheels, stop/go games, vehicle books, sounds, printing and box construction.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 5 - Things That Move

weeks.title: Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility
weeks.notes: Responsive review rather than formal examination.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

items.title: Review and responsive curriculum
items.learningContent:
No formal examination. Revisit weather, clothing, helpers, tools, transport, movement, vocabulary, Practical Life, books, songs and
routines. Review whether vocabulary, participation, routine anticipation and independent attempts have increased and plan
responsively.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.assessmentFocus:
Review whether vocabulary, participation, routine anticipation and independent attempts have increased and plan
responsively.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

weeks.title: Journeys and Places
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children connect movement with familiar destinations.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 7 - Journeys and Places

items.title: Position, movement and familiar journeys
items.learningIntent: Children connect movement with familiar destinations.
items.learningContent:
Children connect movement with familiar destinations. Vocabulary: go, come, home, school, road, market, car, bus, near, far, here,
there. Explore in/out, on/off, near/far, forward/back and under/over physically. Use familiar local photographs, journey stories,
tracks and travel-bag Practical Life. Character: Patience.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use familiar local photographs, journey stories,
tracks and travel-bag Practical Life.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.parentHomeConnection:
Vocabulary: go, come, home, school, road, market, car, bus, near, far, here,
there.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 7 - Journeys and Places

weeks.title: Food I Know
weeks.mainDevelopment: Food vocabulary, senses and healthy experiences
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children explore familiar foods through language, senses, classification and Practical Life.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 8 - Food I Know

items.title: Food vocabulary, senses and healthy experiences
items.learningIntent: Children explore familiar foods through language, senses, classification and Practical Life.
items.learningContent:
Children explore familiar foods through language, senses, classification and Practical Life. Vocabulary includes food, eat, drink,
fruit, water, rice, yam, bread, banana, orange, sweet, soft, hard. Mealtimes support choice, communication and independence.
Explore one/more, full/empty, big/small and sorting. Practical Life: wash suitable fruit, transfer, serve and wipe. Character:
Gratitude.
items.practicalLife: wash suitable fruit, transfer, serve and wipe
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 8 - Food I Know

weeks.title: Farms and Markets
weeks.mainDevelopment: Food origins and Nigerian community life
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children begin connecting familiar foods with places and people involved in producing and selling them.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 9 - Farms and Markets

items.title: Food origins and Nigerian community life
items.learningIntent: Children begin connecting familiar foods with places and people involved in producing and selling them.
items.learningContent:
Children begin connecting familiar foods with places and people involved in producing and selling them. Vocabulary: farm, farmer,
market, food, fruit, vegetable, chicken, goat, buy, basket. Use local market scenes and produce. Introduce farmer grows -> market
sells -> family buys -> we eat through experience, without requiring verbal reproduction. Use basket sorting, market role play and
transfer work. Character: Thankfulness and Respect for Work.
items.teachingGuidance: Use local market scenes and produce.
items.nigerianAfricanContext: Use local market scenes and produce.
items.parentHomeConnection:
Introduce farmer grows -> market
sells -> family buys -> we eat through experience, without requiring verbal reproduction.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 9 - Farms and Markets

weeks.title: Building and Making
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children investigate joining, stacking, filling, fitting, knocking down and rebuilding.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 10 - Building and Making

items.title: Materials, construction and problem-solving
items.learningIntent: Children investigate joining, stacking, filling, fitting, knocking down and rebuilding.
items.learningContent:
Children investigate joining, stacking, filling, fitting, knocking down and rebuilding. Vocabulary: build, block, tall, fall, up, down, on,
inside, more, again. Explore size, position, fit, space and simple comparison through blocks, boxes, loose parts, dough and collage.
Adults allow attempt, collapse, retry, repetition and problem-solving. Character: Perseverance.
items.teachingGuidance: Adults allow attempt, collapse, retry, repetition and problem-solving.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 10 - Building and Making

weeks.title: Nigeria: My Home
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children develop positive cultural belonging through familiar experiences rather than geography memorisation.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 11 - Nigeria: My Home

items.title: Identity, culture, music and environment
items.learningIntent: Children develop positive cultural belonging through familiar experiences rather than geography memorisation.
items.learningContent:
Children develop positive cultural belonging through familiar experiences rather than geography memorisation. Vocabulary: Nigeria,
home, family, music, food, clothes, flag. Experience Nigerian music, foods, clothing, stories, people, landscapes and everyday life,
including Owo and Ondo State. Explore fabric patterns, colour matching, music and movement. Character: Respect.
items.teachingGuidance: Children develop positive cultural belonging through familiar experiences rather than geography memorisation.
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Vocabulary: Nigeria,
home, family, music, food, clothes, flag.
items.parentHomeConnection:
Vocabulary: Nigeria,

weeks.title: Music, Art and Celebration
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children communicate and create through sound, movement, colour and materials.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 12 - Music, Art and Celebration

items.title: Creative expression and cultural experience
items.learningIntent: Children communicate and create through sound, movement, colour and materials.
items.learningContent:
Children communicate and create through sound, movement, colour and materials. Vocabulary: sing, dance, drum, loud, quiet, fast,
slow, colour, make. Explore dance, clapping, stamping, repeated beats, drumming, call-and-response, painting, collage and
construction. Include appropriate Yoruba and Nigerian songs alongside wider children's repertoire. Character: Joy and Community.
items.nigerianAfricanContext: Include appropriate Yoruba and Nigerian songs alongside wider children's repertoire.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 12 - Music, Art and Celebration

weeks.title: Look What I Can Do
weeks.curriculumIntent: The final week makes development visible through participation rather than testing.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Second Term / Week 13 - Look What I Can Do

items.title: Reflection, independence and term closure
items.learningIntent: The final week makes development visible through participation rather than testing.
items.learningContent:
The final week makes development visible through participation rather than testing. Revisit favourite stories, songs, materials,
Practical Life, movement, construction, nature, role play and outdoor experiences. Review Communication & Language, PSED,
Physical Development, Literacy, Mathematics, Understanding the World, Expressive Arts and Practical Life/independence.
items.teachingGuidance: The final week makes development visible through participation rather than testing.
items.outdoorLearning:
Revisit favourite stories, songs, materials,
Practical Life, movement, construction, nature, role play and outdoor experiences.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.assessmentFocus:
Review Communication & Language, PSED,
Physical Development, Literacy, Mathematics, Understanding the World, Expressive Arts and Practical Life/independence.
